Consult Summary:
- Suspected acute respiratory infection with nasal symptoms and dry cough in a patient with hypertension and diabetes; managed supportively with instructions to monitor and follow up if red flags develop.

History:
- Presenting complaint: About 5 days of cough (dry, frequent) and runny nose with persistent nasal discharge described as green; no productive sputum, chest pain, shortness of breath, or hemoptysis.
- Symptom timeline: Onset ~5 days ago; cough remains persistent; temperature fluctuations with hot/cold sensations but no measured fever; some throat comfort from lemon sips; no vomiting or diarrhea currently.
- Exposures/relievers: Lemon sips used (2–3 per day) and reported to soothe throat and aid sleep.
- Associated symptoms: Feeling hot with chills; no headaches, vision changes, rash, or ear pain.
- Past Medical History: Hypertension; type 2 diabetes.
- Medications: Metformin; Lisinopril (dose noted as 200; route/frequency not documented); Lemsip (paracetamol-containing) used 2–3 times daily (dose not documented); no home blood glucose monitoring equipment reported.
- Allergies: Hay fever (seasonal); no drug allergies reported.
- Social History: Lives with partner and dog; works as office manager; alcohol use described as occasional; smoking status not documented.
- Family History: Not mentioned.
- Weight/Height: Height 5'5"; Weight 65 kg.
- Travel/others: Not discussed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute respiratory infection with nasal symptoms and dry cough (likely viral)
  - Plan:
    - Reassurance that most infections are viral and self-limiting; may take 1–2 weeks; cough can persist longer.
    - Self-monitoring: take ambient temperature with a thermometer; seek care if temperature remains elevated (≥37.5–38°C or higher) or if fever persists/worsens, cough worsens, thick/green phlegm is produced, hemoptysis, or shortness of breath.
    - Treatment/support: continue lemon sips; avoid additional paracetamol-containing products while using Lemsip; cough syrup not advised during the daytime; if sleep is significantly disrupted, limited nighttime cough syrup may be used to help sleep.
    - Diabetes considerations: higher risk of bacterial infection; re-evaluate with PCP if symptoms do not settle.
    - Follow-up: re-consult if red flags or no improvement.
- Issue 2: Hypertension and diabetes management
  - Plan:
    - Continue current medications: metformin and lisinopril.
    - Monitoring: schedule and attend regular BP and diabetes checkups with primary care; patient does not currently have home glucose monitoring equipment.
- General plan:
  - Return to care if worsening symptoms or new red flags; maintain hydration; continue symptomatic care as described.
  - Consider antibiotics only if symptoms fail to settle or worsen after review.
